name: Connecting images and text
gist: Teaching models to understand the relationship between what they see in images and what words mean, so they answer questions and describe pictures accurately.
explain: The foundation of multimodal AI is simple but very useful: can a model learn that an image and a sentence belong together? Picture a training process where you show the model millions of pairs — a photo of a dog and the caption 'a golden retriever running' — and train it to recognize which pairings make sense and which ones don't. This is harder than it sounds because the model needs to understand not just what objects are in the image but what the words mean and how they relate. The model can't just match pixels; it has to grasp that 'running' refers to motion and that 'golden retriever' describes a specific breed, then check if those concepts match what the picture shows.

The challenge is that images and text live in such different spaces. An image is a grid of colors. Text is a sequence of symbols with grammar and context. There is no obvious way to compare them — you can't subtract one from the other or measure distance between them directly. Researchers solve this by projecting both into a shared mathematical space, a hidden layer where both images and text are represented as lists of numbers. Then two things are 'close' if their number vectors are similar. But building this mapping is delicate: you want similar images and captions to land near each other, and mismatched pairs to land far apart, across millions of examples.

The work in this space tackles both directions. Some models learn to take an image and generate a fitting description, predicting the next word over and over until the caption is complete. Others take a question and an image and predict the answer — this is called visual question answering, and it requires the model to understand both the question (what is it asking?) and the image (what do I see?) and then reason over them together. Some focus on the alignment itself: given an image and multiple possible captions, pick the right one, or rank them by how well they fit. All of these require the model to build a deep, shared understanding of what images mean and what words mean, so it can link them reliably.

papers.contribution: Achieves strong grounding performance without task-specific fine-tuning, substantially reducing reliance on annotated data.

papers.title: UALM: Unified Audio Language Model for Understanding, Generation and Reasoning
papers.contribution: Matches state-of-the-art specialized models while demonstrating first cross-modal generative reasoning in audio with effectiveness confirmed by evaluations.

papers.title: Uncovering Grounding IDs: How External Cues Shape Multi-Modal Binding
papers.contribution: Grounding IDs improve cross-modal alignment, reduce hallucinations, and enhance attention between related components, demonstrating that external cues are a key mechanism for improving LVLM multimodal reasoning.

papers.title: UniPercept: Towards Unified Perceptual-Level Image Understanding across Aesthetics, Quality, Structure, and Texture
papers.contribution: Establishes the first unified framework and benchmark for perceptual-level image understanding with a strong baseline that outperforms existing MLLMs and can serve as a reward model for text-to-image generation.

papers.title: UniSS: Unified Expressive Speech-to-Speech Translation with Your Voice
papers.contribution: Outperforms prior methods in translation fidelity and quality while preserving voice/emotion/duration; includes 44.8k-hour UniST dataset.

papers.title: Unveiling the Visual Counting Bottleneck in Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: The work identifies the Fractured Magnitude Hypothesis—VLMs learn disjoint, modality-specific statistical manifolds preventing cross-modal grounding for unseen pairings—and shows this affects state-of-the-art foundation models.

papers.title: V-ABS: Action-Observer Driven Beam Search for Dynamic Visual Reasoning
papers.contribution: Achieves 19.7% average improvement on Qwen3-VL-8B and consistent gains across open-source and proprietary models on eight benchmarks.

papers.title: VGR: Visual Grounded Reasoning
papers.contribution: Achieves superior performance on multimodal benchmarks using only 30% of image tokens: +4.1 on MMStar, +7.1 on AI2D, +12.9 on ChartQA.

papers.title: VL-JEPA: Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Vision-language
papers.contribution: VL-JEPA achieves stronger performance than CLIP and SigLIP2 with 50% fewer parameters; supports selective decoding for 2.85x fewer operations; matches VLMs on VQA with only 1.6B parameters.

papers.title: VR-Thinker: Boosting Multimodal Reward Models through Think with Image Reasoning
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on video benchmarks: 80.5% on VideoGen Reward, 82.3% on GenAI-Bench, and 75.6% on MJ-Bench-Video with a 7B model.

papers.title: Variational Adapter for Cross-modal Similarity Representation
papers.contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness on image-text retrieval, domain generalization, and base-to-novel generalization with robust generalization ability.

papers.title: Very Efficient Listwise Multimodal Reranking for Long Documents
papers.contribution: ZipRerank matches or surpasses state-of-the-art multimodal rerankers while reducing inference latency by up to an order of magnitude.

papers.title: ViPER: Empowering the Self-Evolution of Visual Perception Abilities in Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Achieves average 1.7% gain on seven benchmarks with up to 6.0% improvement on fine-grained perception while maintaining generalizability.

papers.title: VisCodex: Unified Multimodal Code Generation via Merging Vision and Coding Models
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art among open-source MLLMs approaching proprietary models like GPT-4o on visually-rich programming tasks.

papers.title: VisuRiddles: Fine-grained Perception is a Primary Bottleneck for Multimodal Large Language Models in Abstract Visual Reasoning
papers.contribution: PAVR substantially outperforms open-source and commercial MLLMs, demonstrating fine-grained perception as the primary bottleneck in abstract visual reasoning.

papers.title: Visual Self-Refine: A Pixel-Guided Paradigm for Accurate Chart Parsing
papers.contribution: ChartVSR achieves strong chart parsing performance by decomposing the task into iterative Refine Stage for accurate pixel localizations and Decode Stage using visual anchors.

papers.title: Vlaser: Vision-Language-Action Model with Synergistic Embodied Reasoning
papers.contribution: Vlaser achieves state-of-the-art on embodied reasoning benchmarks and competitive performance on WidowX and Google Robot benchmarks.

papers.title: WebWatcher: Breaking New Frontiers of Vision-Language Deep Research Agent
papers.contribution: WebWatcher outperforms text-centric agents and open-source baselines on the BrowseComp-VL benchmark, demonstrating superior perception and multimodal reasoning capabilities.

papers.title: World Guidance: World Modeling in Condition Space for Action Generation
papers.contribution: WoG significantly outperforms future-prediction methods with superior generalization, learning effectively from substantial human manipulation videos across simulation and real-world environments.

papers.title: cadrille: Multi-modal CAD Reconstruction with Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: cadrille sets new state-of-the-art on DeepCAD benchmark across three modalities and four datasets, including real-world data.
